answer: Each agent could earn influence only by completing tasks whose results are independently checked and whose rewards vest gradually. A new identity starts with no reputation or claim on past work, so splitting one operator across many accounts does not multiply trusted output. To build influence, the attacker must produce useful work that passes review and wait for rewards to vest; fabricated submissions risk rejection and wasted effort. An atlas of task histories can expose an echo of copied work, while a zenith of influence remains costly to reach.
